clusters.summary: quoteIdentifierIfNecessary(vars[0]) is called with undefined when the SQL expression has no sibling query, so isValidIdentifier's toUpperCase throws a TypeError and the editor crashes on render where it previously rendered 'FROM undefined'.
clusters.rationale: ExpressionQueryEditor.tsx:118 and alerting Expression.tsx:101 build refIds by filtering out only the current query, so vars[0] is undefined when the SQL expression is alone; sqlUtil.ts:53-54 then does regex.test(undefined) (true for 'undefined') followed by undefined.toUpperCase(), a TypeError on render where the old code rendered 'FROM undefined' — exactly thread 0.

clusters.summary: The alerting DAG's cleanTableName strips quotes and parens but not backticks and truncates at the first space, so backtick-quoted FROM targets no longer match any refId, Graph.link throws, and the SQL expression is dropped from the alert graph.
clusters.rationale: cleanTableName strips only `'"()` and then splits at the first space, so a `FROM \`gdp per capita\`` target becomes "`gdp", graph.link throws (dag.ts:162) and createDAGFromQueriesSafe drops the SQL expression in the alerting rule editor; spaced refIds were already unlinkable before, so this is an incomplete fix in the alerting path rather than a strict regression, but the newly generated backticked SQL is still not understood there.

clusters.summary: Core feature code imports quoteIdentifierIfNecessary from the decoupled mysql datasource plugin workspace, coupling core to a plugin internal in the wrong dependency direction.
clusters.rationale: mysql is a decoupled workspace package (public/app/plugins/datasource/mysql/package.json, eslint 'grafana/decoupled-plugins-overrides' zone) and metaSqlExpr.ts already carries a local helper, so importing the plugin's internal sqlUtil into core is a real but non-breaking dependency-direction concern; there is limited precedent (loki types) so it is minor.

clusters.summary: The two new test files fail the repo's CI lint gates: @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any and import/order errors plus prettier --check failures from trailing whitespace and formatting.
clusters.rationale: Verified by running the repo's eslint (14 errors: @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any at those lines plus import/order in metaSqlExpr.test.ts:3) and prettier --check (both new test files flagged); CI-blocking but not a code defect.

clusters.summary: quoteIdentifierIfNecessary wraps identifiers in backticks without doubling embedded backticks, so a refId like a`b yields malformed SQL.
clusters.rationale: quoteIdentifierIfNecessary wraps in backticks without doubling embedded backticks and QueryEditorRowHeader.tsx:51-64 imposes no character restrictions on refIds, so a backtick-containing refId yields malformed SQL; real but a contrived edge case in a pre-existing helper.

clusters.summary: The `refId.label || refId.value || ''` fallback in the completion provider can hand quoteIdentifierIfNecessary an empty string, producing a completion of two bare backticks (reachable only if a refId has neither label nor value).
clusters.rationale: True that '' would become '``', but both callers (ExpressionQueryEditor.tsx:118, alerting Expression.tsx:101-103) always set value and label from a non-empty refId, so the case is unreachable in practice.

clusters.summary: metaSqlExpr.ts binds to a file-local regex-only quoteIdentifierIfNecessary with no reserved-word check while the other call sites use the mysql helper, so reserved-word refIds are quoted in the editor but left bare in the metadata query, which fails and silently empties column autocomplete.
clusters.rationale: metaSqlExpr.ts binds to its file-local regex-only quoteIdentifierIfNecessary (no RESERVED_WORDS check) while SqlExpr.tsx and the completion provider use mysql/sqlUtil's version (sqlUtil.ts:52-56), so a reserved-word refId is quoted in the editor but bare in the metadata query — the inconsistency thread 2 raises.

clusters.summary: The read-back path never unquotes: Monaco tokenizes a backtick-quoted table name into separate tokens so getTableToken yields a lone backtick or quoted name, which fetchSQLFields re-quotes into broken SQL and whose refId filter matches nothing, so column autocomplete silently returns empty for the very refIds this change enables.
clusters.rationale: Monaco's mysql tokenizer emits '`' as a separate identifier.quote token and plugin-ui getTableToken returns the first non-whitespace token after FROM, so fetchSQLFields receives a lone backtick, re-quotes it and its refId filter matches nothing; this is the missing source-query lookup / unquote on the read-back path that thread 7 describes.

clusters.summary: The second completion-provider test wraps all assertions in `if (resolveFunc)` with no expect(resolveFunc).toBeDefined() backstop (and checks only name, not completion), so it can pass with zero assertions and does not protect the changed line.
clusters.rationale: The second test has no expect(resolveFunc).toBeDefined() before its `if (resolveFunc)` block and asserts only `name`, so it can pass with zero assertions and never checks the changed `completion` field.

clusters.summary: plugin-ui appends the ' $0' cursor tab stop only when completion === name, so backtick-quoted table completions lose the trailing placeholder — a cosmetic UX inconsistency.
clusters.rationale: plugin-ui appends ' $0' only when completion === name, so backticked table completions lose the trailing space/cursor stop that unquoted names still get; true and observable, but cosmetic.

clusters.summary: The GenAI suggestion/explain path still passes raw unquoted refIds to the model, so generated SQL for space-containing refIds remains unquoted and fails.
clusters.rationale: SqlExpr passes raw `vars` to SqlQueryActions and the GenAI prompt joins them unquoted (`refIds.join(', ')`), so the AI path was not updated alongside the editor/autocomplete paths; whether the model then emits unquoted SQL is expected LLM behavior, not verifiable, so the impact is uncertain.
